content: The test image shows a corn plant with abnormal growth - there's a mass of dark, tangled tissue (appears to be distorted silks/tassel) with several white/pale oval gall-like structures emerging from it. This looks like a smut disease or crazy top. Let me check reference images.

The Head_smut reference image (top-left panel) is an **exact match** to the test image — dark tangled fibrous tissue (remnant silks/vascular strands) with white/blue oval gall structures embedded within. This is the classic presentation of head smut (*Sphacelotheca reiliana*), which replaces the ear with a mass of dark spores surrounded by a fibrous network, with white immature galls visible.

- **Common_smut**: Shows smooth, round, greenish-white tumors on individual kernels/stalk — different structure
- **Crazy_top**: Shows proliferation of many small leaves at the tassel — no galls present
- **Head_smut**: Dark fibrous mass with embedded white oval galls replacing the ear — **perfect match**

Let me view a few more reference images to confirm this is not something else.

None of the ear rots or downy mildew match — they show visible kernels with mold or leaf yellowing. The test image is unambiguously **Head_smut**: the top-left panel of the Head_smut reference collage is essentially the same photo — dark tangled fibrous mass (persistent silks/vascular tissue) with white/blue oval immature galls replacing the ear, on an otherwise green stalk.
